varieties.name: Sweet Sixteen
varieties.summary: Very sweet, crisp and juicy, with yellow flesh and a striking flavour often likened to cherry candy or sugar cane; anise notes come through after a spell in store. Acidity is low to moderate.

varieties.name: Sweet Society
varieties.summary: A Cox-like apple, sweet, rich and aromatic. The fruit are small, so crops need thinning.

varieties.name: SweeTango
varieties.summary: Explosively crisp and juicy like Honeycrisp, but with a more complex sweet-tart flavour; tasters pick out spicy, citrus-like notes reminiscent of spiced cider. Best eaten early - quality falls off after a few weeks.

varieties.name: Telstar
varieties.summary: Firm, coarse cream flesh with a sweet, rich flavour and only mild acidity; described as strongly flavoured and sweeter than Cox.

varieties.name: Ten Commandments
varieties.summary: Mild and mostly sweet with only gentle tannin; pleasant enough to eat and cook, and in cider it adds a pink tinge. Some tasters note an unusual, almost balsamic flavour.

varieties.name: Tolman Sweet
varieties.summary: Firm, rather dry flesh with an intensely sweet, low-acid flavour; fairly plain raw but prized for baking, boiling and pickling, which bring out its richness. Also used in sweet ciders.

varieties.name: Tom Putt
varieties.summary: Sharp and juicy with a slightly bitter edge when picked, mellowing into a brisk, fragrant eating apple after a few weeks. It cooks well and makes a sharp cider with low tannin.

varieties.name: Tompkins King
varieties.summary: Coarse-grained but crisp, juicy, yellowish flesh with a pleasant balance of sweetness and mild acidity and a rich, lightly floral aroma. Excellent both raw and cooked; it is at its best in autumn and early winter.

varieties.name: Topaz
varieties.summary: Crisp, juicy cream flesh with a bold, tangy sweet-sharp balance, reminiscent of Lord Lambourne or James Grieve but much crunchier. It scores well in tastings with people who like a sharper apple, and the sharpness softens a little in store.

varieties.name: Tower of Glamis
varieties.summary: Crisp, fairly fine, firm greenish-white flesh, juicy with a sharp but distinctly perfumed flavour. Cooks down to a well-flavoured puree.

varieties.name: Transcendent
varieties.summary: Cream-yellow, juicy flesh with a mildly acid but noticeably astringent flavour; it softens quickly. Used for jelly, pickling, sauce and as a tannic addition to cider blends.

varieties.name: Transparente de Croncels
varieties.summary: Juicy, slightly crisp but coarse-grained white-yellow flesh with a mild sweet-sharp flavour and faint aroma. Excellent cooked; eaten fresh it must be taken straight from the tree, as it soon turns mealy.

varieties.name: Tropical Beauty
varieties.summary: Sold as a sweet-tart eating apple for warm climates; reliable independent tasting notes were not found.

varieties.name: Twenty Ounce
varieties.summary: Coarse, fairly tender yellowish flesh with a brisk, mildly acid flavour. Best used for baking, sauce and pies, though acceptable raw when fully ripe.

varieties.name: Tydeman's Early Worcester
varieties.summary: Crisp, fine white flesh that is very juicy, with a sweet, vinous flavour that shows the McIntosh side of its parentage. Short-lived: it softens within a couple of weeks.

varieties.name: Tydeman's Late Orange
varieties.summary: Very firm, crisp and fairly juicy cream flesh with a rich, aromatic flavour in the Cox style. Quite sharp early in the season, it becomes sweeter and more rounded by midwinter.

varieties.name: Virginia Beauty
varieties.summary: Fine-grained, tender, juicy greenish-yellow flesh with a sweet, mild flavour; prized as a late dessert apple that holds well into winter.

varieties.name: Vista Bella
varieties.summary: Light, juicy, creamy-white flesh with a fruity McIntosh-like flavour that reminds some tasters of slightly under-ripe raspberries. Excellent off the tree but loses crispness and flavour within days.

varieties.name: Warner's King
varieties.summary: Juicy, rather soft and coarse greenish flesh with a very sharp acidity. Breaks down quickly into a tart puree when cooked.

varieties.name: Wealthy
varieties.summary: Crisp at first, with tender, very juicy white flesh and a lively, wine-like balance of sugar and acidity; some tasters pick up a faint strawberry note. It softens and loses its zest within a few weeks of picking.

varieties.name: Westfield Seek-No-Further
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp yet tender, juicy flesh with a rich, mild, rather sweet flavour, distinctly aromatic and with a honeyed, nutty depth. A dessert apple of high quality but not recommended for cooking.

varieties.name: Wheeler's Russet
varieties.summary: Greenish-white flesh with a gentle balance of sugar and acid and a light aroma; Victorian writers found it rich and wine-like, especially once the fruit began to shrivel in store. Modern assessments describe it as somewhat soft and only mildly aromatic.

varieties.name: White Transparent
varieties.summary: Brisk and acidic with only a little sweetness, and coarse, juicy white flesh. Very short-lived: within days of picking it turns woolly and dry, so it is best used straight away, raw or cooked to a quick, pale purée.

varieties.name: Wickson Crab
varieties.summary: Startlingly intense: very high sugar matched by high acidity, giving a bright, concentrated sweet-tart flavour in a small, hard, juicy fruit. Excellent eaten fresh and valued for adding sugar and acid to cider.

varieties.name: William Crump
varieties.summary: Firm, fine-textured and juicy, with plenty of sweetness and an intense, rich aromatic flavour drawn from its Cox parent.

varieties.name: Williams' Pride
varieties.summary: Crisp and juicy cream-white flesh with a rich, spicy, sweet-tart flavour that is unusually full for an early apple. Fruit ripens unevenly, so the best are those picked fully ripe and eaten fresh.

varieties.name: Winesap
varieties.summary: Crisp, firm, juicy yellowish flesh with a tangy, spicy and distinctly wine-like flavour, sweet with a sharp finish. Keeps its character for months in store, which is why it was a favourite cider and winter apple.

varieties.name: Winston
varieties.summary: Firm, fine-textured, crisp and juicy cream flesh. It is noticeably sharp at picking and mellows in store to a sweet, aromatic, Cox-like flavour. It keeps its crispness well into spring.

varieties.name: Winter Banana
varieties.summary: Mildly sweet, fairly soft and slightly coarse flesh with a distinctive perfume that many tasters liken to banana, strongest once the fruit has mellowed in store. Acidity is low.

varieties.name: Winter Pearmain
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp, juicy yellowish flesh, sweet with a brisk, pleasant acidity. Usable for both dessert and the kitchen through the winter.

varieties.name: Wolf River
varieties.summary: Soft, rather dry, greenish-white flesh with a mild, modestly acid flavour; undistinguished raw but excellent cooked, where it holds its shape, needs little sugar and gains flavour.

varieties.name: Worcester Pearmain
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp white flesh that is sweet rather than sharp. Picked early it is dull and hard, but left to ripen fully on the tree it develops its well-known strawberry-like, slightly perfumed flavour.

varieties.name: Wyken Pippin
varieties.summary: Tender to moderately firm, fine-grained, very juicy flesh with a sweet, rich, aromatic flavour and a brisk edge. A highly rated old winter dessert apple.

varieties.name: Xanthous
varieties.summary: Not recorded in any independent source available to us.

varieties.name: Yates
varieties.summary: Tender, juicy, aromatic yellowish-white flesh with a pleasant, sweetish flavour; holds its quality through the winter. Good for fresh eating and well regarded for cider.

varieties.name: Yellow Bellflower
varieties.summary: Tender, juicy, fine-grained flesh that is quite tart and aromatic when picked, mellowing to a sweeter, perfumed apple after a few weeks in store. Used for pies early in the season and for eating later.

varieties.name: Yellow Ingestrie
varieties.summary: Fine-textured, tender greenish-yellow flesh with a rich, sweet-sharp and pleasantly aromatic flavour; only moderately juicy.

varieties.name: York Imperial
varieties.summary: Firm, crisp, moderately juicy flesh that is tart-sweet at picking and slowly becomes sweeter and mellower over several months in store. Holds together well in cooking and gives a good sauce.

varieties.name: Young America
varieties.summary: Sharp and noticeably astringent, more like a large crab than a typical dessert apple; an unusual, intense fruit flavour for those who like tartness.

varieties.name: Zabergau Reinette
varieties.summary: Firm, dense and fairly juicy yellowish flesh with a rich, nutty flavour. Sharp and hard straight from the tree, it becomes noticeably sweeter after a month or so in cool storage.

varieties.name: Zestar
varieties.summary: Very crisp, light and juicy - far crunchier than most early apples - with a lively sweet-tart balance and a hint of brown sugar. Keeps its texture much longer than typical summer apples.
